abstract.p: When developing language technology, researchers have routinely turned to transfer learning to solve the data scarcity conundrum presented in low-resource languages. To our knowledge, this study is the first to evaluate the amount of documentation needed for transfer learning, specifically the smallest vocabulary size needed to create a sentence embedding space. In adopting widely spoken languages as a proxy for low-resource languages, our experiments show that the relationship between a sentence embedding's vocabulary size and performance is logarithmic with performance leveling at a vocabulary size of 25,000. It should be noted that this relationship cannot be replicated across all languages, and this level of documentation does not exist for many low-resource languages. We do observe, however, that performance accelerates at a vocabulary size of ≤ 1000, a quantity that is present in most low-resource language documentation. These results can aid researchers in understanding whether a low-resource language has enough documentation necessary to support the creation of a sentence embedding and language model.
